text:
Salem reported 9 licensed child care facilities in 2025
In 2025, Salem was home to 9 licensed child care facilities, according to the Illinois Department of Children and Family Services.
These facilities included 3 day care centers, making up 33.3%, and 6 group day care homes, representing 66.7%.
Salem’s providers care for children from infancy up to age 12, with programs serving infants, toddlers, preschoolers and school-age youth.
All child care providers in Salem offer services in English, with language support available at every facility.
Across Illinois, there were 8,602 licensed child care facilities in 2025.
The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services announced Jan. 6 it has paused certain federal child care and family assistance funding for California, Colorado, Minnesota, New York and Illinois due to concerns of fraud and misuse. The freeze affects nearly $2.4 billion in Child Care and Development Fund grants, $7.35 billion in Temporary Assistance for Needy Families funds and $869 million in Social Services Block Grants, requiring the states to provide documentation before funds are released.
Illinois Gov. J.B. Pritzker criticized the freeze as “wrong and cruel” and suggested the state may contest the federal action, saying that Illinois already implements anti-fraud measures.
The Illinois administration says the temporary freeze could impact an estimated 100,000 families and more than 152,000 children who receive services through the state’s Child Care Assistance Program, in addition to funding for several thousand licensed child care providers and 275 human service organizations.
